data.one_liner: Runs a Flutter app in the background on Android using a foreground service.
data.what_it_does: The plugin starts a foreground Android service with a persistent notification to keep the Dart isolate alive. It also acquires a partial wake lock and can disable battery optimizations to allow continuous execution.
use_when: continuous data sync or messaging that must run when the app is not visible
long‑running network connections that need to survive screen off
avoid_when: iOS or cross‑platform projects that need background support on other platforms
scenarios where a foreground notification would be undesirable
strengths: Handles wake lock and battery‑optimization permissions automatically
Simple API to enable/disable background execution
weaknesses: Requires a persistent notification, which may affect user experience
data.setup_notes: Add FOREGROUND_SERVICE permissions and a <service> entry with appropriate foregroundServiceType in AndroidManifest.xml; call FlutterBackground.initialize with notification config before enabling execution

alternatives.name: firebase_messaging
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides cross‑platform background push notifications without needing a foreground service
